text:
alex chen: Heads up — after pushing kernel 6.4.3 to eu-west-2 GPU fleet (p4s) we started seeing nodes going into repeated reboots and DKMS failures around the nvidia module. Not widespread yet but ~12 nodes unhealthy in the AZ cluster.

oncall-bot: :warning: Alert: gpu-nodepool-eu-west-2 reported 12 node reboots in 15m (triggered by kernel-upgrade-job). See incident id: INC-2026-4220

sophia kim: copy. Which driver/CUDA combo was running on those nodes before the kernel bump?
alex chen: Drivers were 535.86, CUDA 12.1. Kernel before push was 5.15.96 -> we rolled to 6.4.3 via image-builder yesterday morning.

raj patel: Posting sample from one host, DKMS build fail + rmmod errors:
```
DKMS: build output:
make KERNELRELEASE=6.4.3-rt-aws x86_64
...
/var/lib/dkms/nvidia/535.86/build/module/nvidia.ko: symbol version mismatch for 'nv_alloc_pages'
modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'nvidia': Exec format error
rmmod: FATAL: Module nvidia is in use by process 23211
```

emily ng: also seeing GPU hang traces in dmesg on other nodes: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79` then kernel stack with `nvidia_uvm` timeouts. Jobs using NCCL start to hang during all-reduce.

sophia kim: That Xid 79 sequence usually points to driver/kernel ABI mismatch. Did DKMS attempt a rebuild and fail to sign or install?

raj patel: DKMS attempted rebuild but failed due to symbol mismatch. Looks like some kernel headers for the rt/variant didn't match what's in the image. We saw `modpost` warnings about missing versions. CI-bot forced a reimage to the new kernel without matching prebuilt driver.

ci-bot: Automated deploy: kernel-image-6.4.3 -> applied to nodepool-gpu-eu-west-2 at 2026-03-15T09:12:03Z. No driver-package bump.

alex chen: Impact: training clusters in eu-west-2 are retrying and lengthening jobs, autoscaler spun additional nodes in other regions (incurring cross-region egress + cost). Estimated cost delta ~ +18% for spot spend this week.

emily ng: NCCL errors look like `unrecoverable error: ncclAllReduce` on rank 0. When one node's GPU driver dies, the job hangs waiting for collectives. We should isolate affected AZ and failover.

sophia kim: Proposal: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) disable kernel auto-upgrade for remaining pools, 3) roll a small canary rollback to 5.15.96 images for p4 nodes and re-run DKMS with prebuilt modules, 4) notify customers with jobs in-flight. Thoughts?

raj patel: Agree. Also add a quick script to check `modinfo nvidia` output across nodes and `dmesg | grep NVRM` to classify severity before cordoning. I can push an inspection job.

alex chen: Doing inspection now — sample outputs:
```
$ ssh gpu-node-043
$ modinfo nvidia | head -n3
filename:       /lib/modules/6.4.3-rt-aws/kernel/drivers/gpu/nvidia/nvidia.ko
version:        535.86
license:        NVIDIA
$ dmesg | tail -n20
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[  123.457000] kernel: nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol nv_alloc_pages
```

emily ng: We should also watch for tainted kernel flags in `uname -a` + `cat /proc/modules` to detect partial module loads that could later OOM or panic.

oncall-bot: Action assigned: eng-infra oncall (raj patel) — investigate and remediate. Priority: high.

raj patel: Quick checklist I'm executing:
- [x] cordon affected nodes
- [x] disable auto-upgrade job in image-builder for nodepool-gpu-eu-west-2
- [x] run DKMS diagnostics job across pool
- [ ] schedule rollback image bake to 5.15.96 + prebuilt nvidia-535.86 package
- [ ] execute canary rollback (3 nodes)

sophia kim: If rollback is too slow, we can temp patch by installing the distro-provided `nvidia-dkms` package built for 6.4.3 (if available) or force a driver bump to 540.x if that resolves ABI mismatch. But bumping drivers needs QA.

emily ng: For customers: suggest we throttle new training job scheduling to avoid more cross-region autoscaling and hitless job queuing. Also update status page with degraded cluster compute in eu-west-2.

alex chen: Filed tracking issue: https://ourtracker.internal/INFRA-1259 (put details + logs). Please add any extra logs there.

raj patel: Early root-cause hypothesis: image-builder used generic kernel headers that didn't include RT/variant symbols, so DKMS couldn't align symbol versions for prebuilt modules. Repro steps in INFRA-1259.

oncall-bot: Update: rollback canary window scheduled in 30m, engineers oncall/eng-infra/eng-runtime paged.

sophia kim: Thanks. After canary, if stable we will gate rolling upgrade and publish a hotfix image with signed prebuilt nvidia modules.

emily ng: One note — some jobs are multi-AZ; even after cordon they may still see NCCL hangs if peers are in a different AZ. We'll add job-level affinity until cluster stabilizes. :thumbsup:

alex chen: Good. Keep this thread updated with node IDs and outcome of canary. I'll start a short postmortem template after we close the incident.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-4220 marked active.

(10-minute later)

raj patel: Canary rollback results: 3 nodes rolled back -> DKMS modules load correctly, `nvidia-smi` returns GPUs, no new Xid 79 in 15m. Expanding rollback to remaining 9 affected nodes.

emily ng: Monitoring NCCL jobs — several stuck jobs recovered after replacing affected ranks. Still scanning for any residual failures.

sophia kim: Post-incident action items: pin image-builder kernel-header ref, add sanity check in deploy pipeline to verify `modinfo nvidia` post-image, add automated canary to kernel-image rollouts.

alex chen: Closing note: cost impact estimate updated to +12% (autoscaler overprovisioning and cross-region traffic). We'll include numbers in postmortem. :memo:
